tool.name: fasta_uppercase
tool.description: upper-case a FASTA, discarding any pre-existing soft-masking

param.name: input
param.label: Assembly FASTA
param.help: Plain or gzipped. Soft-masked or not.

tool.help:
**fasta_uppercase** — rewrites every sequence line in upper case and leaves header lines exactly as they are.
The lower-case tally uses ``gsub(/[a-z]/, "&")``, which replaces each match with itself and returns the count, so the line is unchanged and counting costs no second pass.
**Header lines are never modified**, and that is the whole correctness argument for the tool. Sequence names are case-sensitive identifiers, so a blanket ``tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]'`` renames every scaffold — ``scaffold_12`` becomes ``SCAFFOLD_12`` — and every downstream join by name then silently finds nothing.
**Why WF-B needs it.** Each masker already upper-cases its own private working copy, so the BED tracks were always computed de novo. ``bedtools maskfasta -soft``, however, lower-cases the union intervals *on top of whatever was already lower-case*. Applied to an assembly that arrives soft-masked — cs10 ships 46.8% masked from NCBI — the published soft-masked FASTA becomes the union of this pipeline's mask and the assembly's own, with no way to tell them apart, while the BED tracks report only the former.
